methodology.micro: Three fresh off processes, three warmups and nine measured samples per case/process; one separately observed process, same cases, nine samples. Timings include performance.now brackets/assertions equally. No benchmark overlaps a suite or another experiment.
methodology.passes: hydrate counts equal full canonical validation passes; hydratedNodes equals property-validation visits. dehydrate counts are canonical serialization-to-envelope passes, not JSON.stringify calls. After also performs M copyEnvelope shape-validation/copy passes per M edits; copies are retained, not free.
methodology.baseline: Current Spike G runtime; before helper delegates to runtime.edit. Page baseline has no adapter. Archived source texts and hashes establish both implementations.
methodology.http: Three fresh windows per mode/provider; SQLite serial existing/attributed, concurrency-12 existing/attributed/off; JSON concurrency-12 attributed. Existing Spike G bounded supervisor/harness, separate client, 1,000 ms Page deadline. Sequential before/after, no reliability inference from micro speed.

exclusions: Initial benchmark fixture incorrectly compared normalized null-prototype JSON objects with ordinary objects; fixed before all captures.
Restricted-sandbox HTTP workers failed before usable request capture; excluded. Restricted-sandbox node:test produced no usable child results. Native runs replace these attempts.
Initial regression fixtures had two incorrect lifecycle expectations (spread contexts share a fence; ending context can reject Page finalization). Corrected without runtime changes.
limitations: No OS isolation proof from mocks; installed Linux boundary tests are separately recorded.
Host scheduling/load, filesystem, GC and warmup variance remain. Inclusive synchronous spans overlap and cannot be summed as CPU.
Micro contexts have no installed lifetime guard. Their live context checks are counted, not a package-integrity qualification.
Only the two server Page edit sites are optimized. Shared controller, systemSet, package mutation and portable/client edits retain their previous passes.
Observer overhead is reported separately; attributed HTTP absolute timings are perturbed. Failed Pages perform unequal work.
No production deployment, browser manual, hostile-root filesystem, power-loss or network-filesystem qualification.
